text: Four seconds, a progressive pass, and absolutely no initiative to alter the structure through asymmetrical full-back movements into more advanced areas, in sync with the ball’s progression. On several occasions on Saturday, I noticed that the wingers were left isolated, forced to take on two or three opposition players themselves, despite there being fairly good opportunities for the full-backs to make overlapping runs. This often left Liverpool numerically disadvantaged in key areas, allowing Brentford to defend comfortably by maintaining their numerical superiority. There was no tension created no attempt to draw defenders out of position and no expansion of our attacking options. This passive approach to full-back play needs to be eliminated as soon as possible, because it kills potentially dangerous attacking patterns #LFC
label: tactical_analysis
